cold_email.subject: Interest in Full Time Educator / Seasonal Contract / 16310- Jordan Creek — biology/bioinformatics graduate
cold_email.body:
Dear lululemon Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Full Time Educator / Seasonal Contract / 16310- Jordan Creek opportunity with lululemon at lululemon.

I am especially interested in the team's use of quantitative and computational methods to answer meaningful biological questions. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, my background in biology, bioinformatics, Python, R, SQL, Linux, and reproducible workflow development aligns well with that kind of cross-disciplinary work.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. I would be grateful for a 15–20 minute conversation to learn more about the lab's current priorities and discuss where my background could be useful. I have attached my resume for context.

Best,
Celina Lin

cold_email.subject: Interest in Research Associate, Library — biology/bioinformatics graduate
cold_email.body:
Dear Third Bridge Group Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Research Associate, Library opportunity with Third Bridge Group at Third Bridge Group.

I am especially interested in the team's use of quantitative and computational methods to answer meaningful biological questions. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, my background in biology, bioinformatics, Python, R, SQL, Linux, and reproducible workflow development aligns well with that kind of cross-disciplinary work.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. I would be grateful for a 15–20 minute conversation to learn more about the lab's current priorities and discuss where my background could be useful. I have attached my resume for context.

Best,
Celina Lin
https://linkedin.com/in/celina-g-lin

cold_email.subject: Interest in Training and Development Coordinator Job Details / Owens Corning — biology/bioinformatics graduate
cold_email.body:
Dear Owens Corning Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Training and Development Coordinator Job Details / Owens Corning opportunity with Owens Corning at Owens Corning.

I am especially interested in the team's use of quantitative and computational methods to answer meaningful biological questions. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, my background in biology, bioinformatics, Python, R, SQL, Linux, and reproducible workflow development aligns well with that kind of cross-disciplinary work.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. I would be grateful for a 15–20 minute conversation to learn more about the lab's current priorities and discuss where my background could be useful. I have attached my resume for context.

Best,
Celina Lin
https://linkedin.com/in/celina-g-lin

cold_email.body:
Dear Google Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Silicon Engineer, PhD, University Graduate, 2027 Start opportunity with Google at Google.

I am especially interested in the team's use of quantitative and computational methods to answer meaningful biological questions. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, my background in biology, bioinformatics, Python, R, SQL, Linux, and reproducible workflow development aligns well with that kind of cross-disciplinary work.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. I would be grateful for a 15–20 minute conversation to learn more about the lab's current priorities and discuss where my background could be useful. I have attached my resume for context.

Best,
Celina Lin

cold_email.subject: Interest in Player Development Professional — biology/bioinformatics graduate
cold_email.body:
Dear Diamond Run Golf Club Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Player Development Professional opportunity with Diamond Run Golf Club at Diamond Run Golf Club.

I am especially interested in the team's use of quantitative and computational methods to answer meaningful biological questions. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, my background in biology, bioinformatics, Python, R, SQL, Linux, and reproducible workflow development aligns well with that kind of cross-disciplinary work.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. I would be grateful for a 15–20 minute conversation to learn more about the lab's current priorities and discuss where my background could be useful. I have attached my resume for context.

Best,
Celina Lin
https://linkedin.com/in/celina-g-lin

Dear lululemon Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Educator / HYDE PARK VILLAGE opportunity with lululemon at lululemon.

I am especially interested in the team's use of quantitative and computational methods to answer meaningful biological questions. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, my background in biology, bioinformatics, Python, R, SQL, Linux, and reproducible workflow development aligns well with that kind of cross-disciplinary work.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. Celina Lin

cold_email.subject: Interest in Leominster MA Personal Care Management Skills Trainer — biology/bioinformatics graduate
cold_email.body:
Dear Tempus Unlimited, Inc. Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Leominster MA Personal Care Management Skills Trainer opportunity with Tempus Unlimited, Inc. at Tempus Unlimited, Inc..

I am especially interested in the team's use of quantitative and computational methods to answer meaningful biological questions. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, my background in biology, bioinformatics, Python, R, SQL, Linux, and reproducible workflow development aligns well with that kind of cross-disciplinary work.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. I would be grateful for a 15–20 minute conversation to learn more about the lab's current priorities and discuss where my background could be useful. I have attached my resume for context.

Best,
Celina Lin

cold_email.subject: Interest in Clinical Sciences Lab Coordinator — biology/bioinformatics graduate
cold_email.body:
Dear Rocky Vista University Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Clinical Sciences Lab Coordinator opportunity with Rocky Vista University at Rocky Vista University.

I am especially interested in the team's use of quantitative and computational methods to answer meaningful biological questions. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, my background in biology, bioinformatics, Python, R, SQL, Linux, and reproducible workflow development aligns well with that kind of cross-disciplinary work.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. I would be grateful for a 15–20 minute conversation to learn more about the lab's current priorities and discuss where my background could be useful. I have attached my resume for context.

Best,
Celina Lin

cold_email.subject: Interest in Clinical Lab Scientist/MT I — biology/bioinformatics graduate
cold_email.body:
Dear OSF HealthCare Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Clinical Lab Scientist/MT I opportunity with OSF HealthCare at OSF HealthCare.

I am especially interested in the team's use of quantitative and computational methods to answer meaningful biological questions. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, my background in biology, bioinformatics, Python, R, SQL, Linux, and reproducible workflow development aligns well with that kind of cross-disciplinary work.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. I would be grateful for a 15–20 minute conversation to learn more about the lab's current priorities and discuss where my background could be useful. I have attached my resume for context.

Best,
Celina Lin

I am especially interested in the team's use of quantitative and computational methods to answer meaningful biological questions. Best,
Celina Lin

cold_email.subject: Interest in People & Culture Coordinator — biology/bioinformatics graduate
cold_email.body:
Dear Columbia Hospitality Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the People & Culture Coordinator opportunity with Columbia Hospitality at Columbia Hospitality.

I am especially interested in the team's use of quantitative and computational methods to answer meaningful biological questions. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, my background in biology, bioinformatics, Python, R, SQL, Linux, and reproducible workflow development aligns well with that kind of cross-disciplinary work.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. I would be grateful for a 15–20 minute conversation to learn more about the lab's current priorities and discuss where my background could be useful. I have attached my resume for context.

Best,
Celina Lin

cold_email.subject: Interest in Data Center Technical Trainer, Data Center Communities (DCC) — biology/bioinformatics graduate
cold_email.body:
Dear Amazon Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Data Center Technical Trainer, Data Center Communities (DCC) opportunity with Amazon at Amazon.

I am especially interested in the team's use of quantitative and computational methods to answer meaningful biological questions. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, my background in biology, bioinformatics, Python, R, SQL, Linux, and reproducible workflow development aligns well with that kind of cross-disciplinary work.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. I would be grateful for a 15–20 minute conversation to learn more about the lab's current priorities and discuss where my background could be useful. I have attached my resume for context.

Best,
Celina Lin

cold_email.subject: Interest in Business Admin I — biology/bioinformatics graduate
cold_email.body:
Dear NASA Jet Propulsion Laboratory Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Business Admin I opportunity with NASA Jet Propulsion Laboratory at NASA Jet Propulsion Laboratory.

I am especially interested in the team's use of quantitative and computational methods to answer meaningful biological questions. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, my background in biology, bioinformatics, Python, R, SQL, Linux, and reproducible workflow development aligns well with that kind of cross-disciplinary work.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. I would be grateful for a 15–20 minute conversation to learn more about the lab's current priorities and discuss where my background could be useful. I have attached my resume for context.

Best,
Celina Lin
https://linkedin.com/in/celina-g-lin

cold_email.subject: Interest in Seasonal Summer Employment — biology/bioinformatics graduate
cold_email.body:
Dear Mosquito Squad Plus Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Seasonal Summer Employment opportunity with Mosquito Squad Plus at Mosquito Squad Plus.

I am especially interested in the team's use of quantitative and computational methods to answer meaningful biological questions. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, my background in biology, bioinformatics, Python, R, SQL, Linux, and reproducible workflow development aligns well with that kind of cross-disciplinary work.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. I would be grateful for a 15–20 minute conversation to learn more about the lab's current priorities and discuss where my background could be useful. I have attached my resume for context.

Best,
Celina Lin
https://linkedin.com/in/celina-g-lin

jobs.title: Manager, Patient Data Management
jobs.description: Career Category Marketing Job Description Manager, Patient Data Management Job Summary The Manager, Patient Data Management will be responsible for the governance, operation, quality, and strategic management of patient-level data assets supporting Amgen’s Patient Support Programs (PSPs), Specialty Pharmacies (SPs), Site of Care (SOC), and other patient-related data sources. This role partners closely with Commercial, Patient Access, Technology, Privacy, Compliance, Legal, and external vendors to ensure compliant data acquisition, integration, stewardship, and delivery of high-quality patient data that supports business decision-making and patient journey analytics. The role will also serve as a subject matter expert for patient data, helping business and analytics stakeholders understand data definitions, source-system differences, business rules, data limitations, and impacts to downstream reporting and analytics. Key Responsibilities Manage patient data governance and day-to-day operations across Amgen brands and patient support programs, including Hub Services, Nurse Support, Copay, Specialty Pharmacy, Site of Care, and other patient-level data sources. Partner with the Patient Data Management Senior Manager and business stakeholders to gather, document, prioritize, and implement requirements for new patient data sources and enhancements. Lead end-to-end onboarding of patient data sources, including requirements definition, field mapping, File Interface Agreements (FIAs), testing, validation, and production deployment. Review and validate FIAs, file layouts, data mappings, business rules, data-transfer requirements, and source-to-target transformations for new feeds and migration initiatives. Manage external data aggregators, vendors, and technology partners to ensure adherence to data quality, service-level, and operational expectations. Investigate and resolve patient data quality issues through profiling, validation, reconciliation, root-cause analysis, and preventative controls. Develop and maintain data specifications, data dictionaries, business rules, process documentation, governance artifacts, and lineage for patient-level data assets. Provide proactive communication and change management for major patient-data changes, including source or table changes, milestones, downstream impacts, and reporting readiness. Partner with Specialty Pharmacy, Site of Care, Trade & Channel, Contracting, Legal, Privacy, Compliance, Technology, and other functions to establish, review, and operationalize patient data agreements and amendments. Lead Site of Care patient-data operations, including vendor onboarding, data requirements, feed monitoring, data-quality and contract-compliance oversight, issue escalation, and reliable downstream delivery. Respond to complex stakeholder data inquiries and translate business needs into actionable patient-level data requirements, extracts, and analyses involving enrollment, status, brand, claims, payer/coverage, and other patient attributes. Serve as a trusted patient-data subject matter expert and point of contact for data definitions, source-system differences, limitations, data-quality investigations, onboarding, and reporting readiness. Ensure compliant processing, storage, access, and use of patient-level data in alignment with Amgen Privacy, Compliance, Legal, and Information Security policies, including access controls and audit readiness. Support connected patient datasets and Patient 360 initiatives by defining linkage requirements, validating data connections, aligning business rules, documenting lineage, and improving the usability of integrated patient data. Drive continuous improvement through scalable data-management practices, including standardized onboarding, data-quality monitoring, status and issue tracking, automation, lineage, traceability, and self-service capabilities. Identify opportunities to leverage AI and automation across patient data operations, including data-quality monitoring, documentation, issue triage, file monitoring, KPI validation, and stakeholder self-service. Basic Qualifications Doctorate degree and 2 years of data management, analytics, sales and marketing operations, healthcare analytics, patient services, specialty pharmacy, and/or value & access experience OR Master's degree and 4 years of data management, analytics, sales and marketing operations, healthcare analytics, patient services, specialty pharmacy, and/or value & access experience OR Bachelor's degree and 6 years of data management, analytics, sales and marketing operations, healthcare analytics, patient services, specialty pharmacy, and/or value & access experience OR Associate's degree and 10 years of data management, analytics, sales and marketing operations, healthcare analytics, patient services, specialty pharmacy, and/or value & access experience OR High School Diploma / GED and 12 years of data management, analytics, sales and marketing operations, healthcare analytics, patient services, specialty pharmacy, and/or value & access experience Preferred Qualifications Experience managing Patient Support Program, Hub, Copay, Specialty Pharmacy, Site of Care, or other patient-level healthcare data assets. Experience supporting Site of Care patient-data operations, vendor feeds, data-quality management, issue resolution, and downstream delivery. Experience with healthcare, pharmaceutical, patient services, commercial, and value & access data processes and contracting. Experience managing third-party data vendors, aggregators, and technology partners. Demonstrated expertise in data governance, stewardship, quality management, and data lifecycle management. Experience defining business requirements, data mappings, file specifications, data dictionaries, business rules, and integration documentation. Strong analytical skills, including patient-level data profiling, reconciliation, validation, anomaly investigation, and root-cause analysis. Experience supporting data migrations, system implementations, and large-scale data integration initiatives, including assessing downstream reporting and analytics impacts. Experience translating complex stakeholder needs into patient-level data requirements, extracts, validation analyses, and actionable insights. Experience with SQL, Databricks, AWS, Tableau, Power BI, or similar data and analytics technologies. Strong project management, communication, stakeholder management, negotiation, and relationship-building skills, with the ability to influence without authority in a matrixed environment. Knowledge of healthcare privacy, patient-level data governance, compliance requirements, Agile delivery, and continuous improvement practices. What you can expect of us As we work to develop treatments that take care of others, we also work to care for your professional and personal growth and well-being. From our competitive benefits to our collaborative culture, we’ll support your journey every step of the way. The expected annual salary range for this role in the U.S. (excluding Puerto Rico) is posted. Actual salary will vary based on several factors including but not limited to, relevant skills, experience, and qualifications. In addition to the base salary, Amgen offers a Total Rewards Plan, based on eligibility, comprising of health and welfare plans for staff and eligible dependents, financial plans with opportunities to save towards retirement or other goals, work/life balance, and career development opportunities that may include: A comprehensive employee benefits package, including a Retirement and Savings Plan with generous company contributions, group medical, dental and vision coverage, life and disability insurance, and flexible spending accounts A discretionary annual bonus program, or for field sales representatives, a sales-based incentive plan Stock-based long-term incentives Award-winning time-off plans Flexible work models where possible. Refer to the Work Location Type in the job posting to see if this applies. Apply now and make a lasting impact with the Amgen team. careers.amgen.com In any materials you submit, you may redact or remove age-identifying information such as age, date of birth, or dates of school attendance or graduation. You will not be penalized for redacting or removing this information. Application deadline Amgen does not have an application deadline for this position; we will continue accepting applications until we receive a sufficient number or select a candidate for the position. Sponsorship Sponsorship for this role is not guaranteed. As an organization dedicated to improving the quality of life for people around the world, Amgen fosters an inclusive environment of ethical, committed and highly accomplished people who respect each other and live the Amgen values to continue advancing science to serve patients. Together, we compete in the fight against serious disease. Amgen is an Equal Opportunity employer. We make all employment decisions without regard to race, color, religion, sex or any other characteristic protected by applicable law. We provide reasonable accommodations to applicants and employees with disabilities, consistent with legal requirements. Please contact us to request accommodation. . jobs.description: About Glean: Glean is the Work AI platform that helps everyone work smarter with AI. What began as the industry’s most advanced enterprise search has evolved into a full-scale Work AI ecosystem, powering intelligent Search, an AI Assistant, and scalable AI agents on one secure, open platform. With over 100 enterprise SaaS connectors, flexible LLM choice, and robust APIs, Glean gives organizations the infrastructure to govern, scale, and customize AI across their entire business - without vendor lock-in or costly implementation cycles. At its core, Glean is redefining how enterprises find, use, and act on knowledge. Its Enterprise Graph and Personal Knowledge Graph map the relationships between people, content, and activity, delivering deeply personalized, context-aware responses for every employee. This foundation powers Glean’s agentic capabilities - AI agents that automate real work across teams by accessing the industry’s broadest range of data: enterprise and world, structured and unstructured, historical and real-time. The result: measurable business impact through faster onboarding, hours of productivity gained each week, and smarter, safer decisions at every level. Recognized by Fast Company as one of the World’s Most Innovative Companies (Top 10, 2025), by CNBC’s Disruptor 50, Bloomberg’s AI Startups to Watch (2026), Forbes AI 50, and Gartner’s Tech Innovators in Agentic AI, Glean continues to accelerate its global impact. With customers across 50+ industries and 1,000+ employees in more than 25 countries, we’re helping the world’s largest organizations make every employee AI-fluent, and turning the superintelligent enterprise from concept into reality. If you’re excited to shape how the world works, you’ll help build systems used daily across Microsoft Teams, Zoom, ServiceNow, Zendesk, GitHub, and many more. You'll be deeply embedded where people get things done. You'll ship agentic capabilities on an open, extensible stack, with the craft and care required for enterprise trust, as we bring Work AI to every employee, in every company. About the Role: Glean is looking for creative engineers to own and launch delightful user facing features. In a rapidly growing startup, this entails developing ideas with product managers and designers to best balance engineering constraints with requirements, delivering intuitive experiences that run in modern mobile and desktop browsers. Compensation offered will be determined by factors such as location, level, job-related knowledge, skills, and experience. Certain roles may be eligible for variable compensation, equity, and benefits. We offer a comprehensive benefits package including competitive compensation, Medical, Vision, and Dental coverage, generous time-off policy, and the opportunity to contribute to your 401k plan to support your long-term goals. When you join, you'll receive a home office improvement stipend, as well as an annual education and wellness stipends to support your growth and wellbeing. We foster a vibrant company culture through regular events, and provide healthy lunches daily to keep you fueled and focused. We are a diverse bunch of people and we want to continue to attract and retain a diverse range of people into our organization. We're committed to an inclusive and diverse company. We do not discriminate based on gender, ethnicity, sexual orientation, religion, civil or family status, age, disability, or race. #LI-HYBRID AI-First Mindset at Glean: At Glean, AI fluency is core to how we work and we're committed to ensuring every new hire feels confident integrating AI into their everyday work. jobs.description: A healthier future. It’s what drives us to innovate. To continuously advance science and ensure everyone has access to the healthcare they need today and for generations to come. Creating a world where we all have more time with the people we love. That’s what makes us Roche. This role is based in the Real-World & Clinical Data Strategy (RWCDS) team which drives data excellence and analytics to power enhanced decision-making and evidence-generation within Roche Product Development. We develop and implement data strategies that unlock the value of clinical, operational, and real-world data to accelerate evidence generation, decision-making, and innovation across PD and beyond. By embedding FAIR principles, advancing data governance, and enabling data productization, RWCDS ensures that data is not only findable and usable, but also a driver of scientific rigor, regulatory readiness, and AI-powered transformation. Through deep partnerships with internal functions and external collaborators, we shape a future-ready data ecosystem that supports personalized healthcare and efficient drug development. The Opportunity: The RWD Scientist plays a key role in generating insights from real-world data to inform clinical development, regulatory strategy, and healthcare decision-making. Your work enables evidence generation across therapeutic areas and supports the responsible and impactful use of real-world data at scale. cold_email.subject: Interest in RWD Scientist — biology/bioinformatics graduate
cold_email.body:
Dear Genentech / Roche Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the RWD Scientist opportunity with Genentech / Roche at Genentech / Roche.

I am especially interested in the team's use of quantitative and computational methods to answer meaningful biological questions. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, my background in biology, bioinformatics, Python, R, SQL, Linux, and reproducible workflow development aligns well with that kind of cross-disciplinary work.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. I would be grateful for a 15–20 minute conversation to learn more about the lab's current priorities and discuss where my background could be useful. I have attached my resume for context.

Best,
Celina Lin
https://linkedin.com/in/celina-g-lin

jobs.title: Project Coordinator
jobs.description: Are you looking to make a meaningful impact in bioprocess development and join a collaborative team dedicated to scientific excellence? As a Project Coordinator , you will drive sample logistics and testing integrity to support critical process validation studies across our global network. In this role, you will work closely with cross-functional technical teams and quality assurance to help deliver life-changing biopharmaceutical products to patients. The Opportunity: Coordinate assigned Process Validation (PV) study samples across technical development teams, internal laboratories, and external contract manufacturing facilities. Ensure the integrity and progress of PV studies by meticulously following protocols, preparing samples, coordinating submissions, and accurately entering data. Proactively monitor study status, communicate updates to key stakeholders, and guarantee the quality and compliance of all completed work. Review PV protocols and reports for accuracy, completeness, and compliance with regulatory guidelines and internal sample testing standards. Generate, review, and approve PV data summary tables. Perform routine and non-routine analytical testing using techniques such as ELISA, PCR, U/HPLC, CE, LC-MS, and ICP-MS according to established protocols. Actively engage in clear and impactful communication across all organizational levels and escalate PV issues at team and department meetings to drive resolution. Attend PV and project meetings to represent the analytical operations team and ensure cross-functional alignment. Who you are: You hold a Bachelor's degree in Life Sciences or a related field. You have a minimum of 1 year of laboratory experience in biotechnology or a related area, along with knowledge of analytical methodologies. You possess familiarity and working knowledge of GxP, including documentation and compliance standards. You demonstrate meticulous attention to detail and a strong commitment to delivering high-quality, compliant work. jobs.title: Biosafety Manager
jobs.description: About Arc Institute Arc Institute is an independent nonprofit research organization at the interface of artificial intelligence and biology, working to accelerate scientific progress and understand the root causes of complex diseases. Founded in 2021 and based in Palo Alto, Arc partners with Stanford University, UC Berkeley, and UC San Francisco. Unlike academia, our scientists have long-term funding and industry-like resources. Unlike industry, they're free to pursue high-risk, long-term research without commercial pressures. Arc's Technology Centers and Core Investigator labs work side by side, integrating experimental and computational biology under one roof to tackle problems neither could solve alone. Our two Institute Initiatives reflect this model in action: Virtual Cell Initiative : Building a full-stack virtual cell model to identify disease mechanisms and nominate drug targets, accelerating the path from biological insight to clinical trials. Alzheimer's Disease Initiative : Mapping the genes, pathways, and environmental factors behind Alzheimer's disease to develop drug candidates that address root causes. More than 300 Arconauts work together at our Palo Alto headquarters, backed by substantial long-term philanthropic funding. About the position As Biosafety Manager, you will be responsible for developing, implementing, supporting, administering, and managing Arc's Biosafety Program. As an experienced biosafety specialist, you will combine biosafety subject-matter expertise with the ability to independently address a broad range of difficult problems. About you You thrive on building and translating regulations and risk assessments into a robust, consistent, and administratively user-friendly Biosafety Program for Arc. You are genuinely curious about our science and driven by a desire to understand our research on a deeper level. You are excited to build programs and foster cross-functional partnerships, helping to strengthen our community and support our mission. In this position you will Establish and lead the Arc Biosafety Program and Institutional Biosafety Committee (IBC) operations to ensure seamless oversight of biological agent usage. Serve as subject matter expert on biological safety for Arc's researchers, representing Arc to local, state, and federal authorities on biosafety matters; provide input to regulators on the development and revision of regulations. Act as primary point of contact for IBC protocol review: assess all research protocols involving biohazards or potentially biohazardous materials, provide pre-review guidance to researchers, and manage approvals and renewals to keep documentation aligned with regulatory requirements. Validate ongoing biosafety program compliance through site inspections and follow-up on biological use authorizations. Advise on biosafety requirements for proposed research, work, and facilities; provide technical guidance on permitting and shipping of biological materials and material transfer agreements (MTAs). Design, deliver, and evaluate biosafety training, including employee onboarding, and keep the biosafety manual and related materials current with practice and regulation. Participate on relevant committees (e.g., IACUC) as an EH&S/biosafety resource. Maintain on-call availability to respond to emergencies (e.g., spills), directing or performing field response as needed. In addition to core biosafety duties, this role provides support and serves as backup coverage across Arc’s general EH&S program, including: Serve as one of two EH&S leaders at Arc, providing shared safety leadership and subject matter expertise aligned with Arc Institute’s operating principles, and advising the administrative team on safety and compliance for specific projects and operations. Help maintain EH&S programs, procedures, and tracking systems (chemical inventories, SDS, near-miss reporting, permits) in compliance with federal, state, and local regulations, and lend expertise to programs such as the Cal/OSHA bloodborne pathogens standard, chemical safety, radiation safety, and controlled substances.Support delivery of EH&S employee safety and onboarding training, with a focus on efficiency and engagement. Contribute to environmental compliance, including the industrial wastewater discharge permit, hazardous waste requirements, and regulatory permitting; serve as backup for regulated hazardous waste programs and vendor contracting, and as backup point of contact for regulatory and certifying agencies. Participate in risk assessments, safety audits, inspections, and walkthroughs across Arc’s labs to identify chemical, physical, biological, and radiological hazards; help remediate them and recommend continuous improvements. Investigate accidents, incidents, injuries, and complaints concerning potential hazards or unsafe conditions to determine root causes and preventive measures. Help coordinate procurement and maintenance of safety equipment and supply inventory, and respond to emergency situations involving hazardous materials. Requirements 5+ years of laboratory experience, including 3+ years in Environmental Health & Safety (EH&S) and Biosafety with a strong grounding in virology or microbiological sciences. Bachelor's degree in life sciences, biology, microbiology, occupational safety and health, or a related field; Master's degree or PhD preferred. Expert knowledge of biosafety and laboratory safety practices, including biosafety cabinet operation, fume hoods and ventilation, PPE, and chemical safety and storage. Highly organized and detail-oriented, with a proven ability to manage multiple projects efficiently and accurately. Strong interpersonal skills, with a demonstrated ability to prioritize resources, positively influence group behaviors, and work with associates to gain consensus on safety best practices. Advanced written, verbal, and interpersonal communication skills; able to work both independently, with minimal oversight, and as part of a dynamic team, with a positive attitude, a strong sense of urgency, and a bias toward action. Interest in learning new techniques, keeping accurate records, following instructions, and complying with company policies. Preferred Qualifications Advanced degree in a biological, life science, or related field. Certification as a Biosafety Professional (CBSP), Registered Biosafety Professional (RBP), Associate Safety Professional (ASP), or Certified Safety Professional (CSP) Knowledge and experience in Animal Research Occupational Health and Safety. Experience in research with laboratory animals involving biohazardous or hazardous material. The base salary range for this position is $ 127,000 to $157,000 . These amounts reflect the range of base salary that the Institute reasonably would expect to pay a new hire or internal candidate for this position. The actual base compensation paid to any individual for this position may vary depending on factors such as experience, market conditions, education/training, skill level, and whether the compensation is internally equitable, and does not include bonuses, commissions, differential pay, other forms of compensation, or benefits. This position is also eligible to receive an annual discretionary bonus, with the amount dependent on individual and institute performance factors. In addition to the Base Salary and Annual Bonus above, you will be eligible to participate in the Institute’s Compound Cash Grant Program (the “CCGP”). The CCGP is a program designed to offer multi-year cash grants providing for a fixed dollar amount paid out in semi-annual installments to reward employees for staying and contributing to the Institute. As soon as reasonably practical after your start date, you will receive a grant letter describing the terms of your award under the CCGP.

cold_email.subject: Interest in Biosafety Manager — biology/bioinformatics graduate
cold_email.body:
Dear Arc Institute Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Biosafety Manager opportunity with Arc Institute at Arc Institute.

I am especially interested in the group's effort to integrate multi-omic and clinical data with AI for biomarker and therapeutic discovery. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, my background in bioinformatics, pipeline development, and an LLM-assisted competency-mapping project has made me especially interested in rigorous, interpretable AI for biomedical data.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. I would be grateful for a 15–20 minute conversation to learn more about the lab's current priorities and discuss where my background could be useful. I have attached my resume for context.

Best,
Celina Lin
https://linkedin.com/in/celina-g-lin

jobs.description: Career Category Scientific Job Description Join Amgen’s Mission of Serving Patients At Amgen, if you feel like you’re part of something bigger, it’s because you are. Our shared mission—to serve patients living with serious illnesses—drives all that we do. Since 1980, we’ve helped pioneer the world of biotech in our fight against the world’s toughest diseases. With our focus on four therapeutic areas –Oncology, Inflammation, General Medicine, and Rare Disease– we reach millions of patients each year. Amgen is advancing a broad and deep pipeline of medicines to treat cancer, heart disease, inflammatory conditions, rare diseases, and obesity and obesity-related conditions. As a member of the Amgen team, you’ll help make a lasting impact on the lives of patients as we research, manufacture, and deliver innovative medicines to help people live longer, fuller happier lives. Our award-winning culture is collaborative, innovative, and science based. If you have a passion for challenges and the opportunities that lay within them, you’ll thrive as part of the Amgen team. Join us and transform the lives of patients while transforming your career. Scientist, Integrated Computational and Experimental Inflammation Discovery What you will do Let’s do this. Let’s change the world. In this vital role, you will contribute to Inflammation discovery programs by personally designing and executing wet-lab studies and applying computational and AI-enabled approaches to analyze and integrate omics data. You will connect these insights with experimental findings to deepen our understanding of disease biology, prioritize therapeutic targets, and develop and test mechanistic hypotheses in the laboratory. Working with minimal supervision, you will manage defined program components, develop an area of scientific expertise, and communicate data-driven insights that help advance project decisions. Key Responsibilities: Plan and coordinate defined project tasks and activities that support target identification, validation, and progression of Inflammation discovery programs. Design, execute, analyze, and interpret bench/wet lab studies to investigate disease mechanisms and test therapeutic hypotheses with scientific rigor and appropriate urgency. Apply computational, AI-enabled, and data-analytic approaches to generate mechanistic insights, refine experimental design, and integrate findings across data sources. Integrate experimental results with published literature, human genetics, clinical observations, and internal or external datasets to inform ongoing project design. Develop and optimize solutions to technical problems of advanced scope and complexity within an emerging area of expertise. Collaborate across functions and departments, contributing at the project-team level and building constructive relationships with wet-lab, computational, translational, and drug-discovery partners. Organize, interpret, document, and present project data and scientific recommendations within work groups, project teams, and internal scientific forums. Coach or guide others within the work group or project team where appropriate, and contribute to a collaborative culture of scientific curiosity, knowledge sharing, and operational excellence. What we expect of you We are all different, yet we all use our unique contributions to serve patients. The researcher we seek is a Scientist with these qualifications. Basic Qualifications: Doctorate degree OR Master’s degree and 2 years of experience in Immunology, Cell Biology, Molecular Biology, Pharmacology, Biomedical Sciences, Computational Biology, Bioengineering OR Bachelor’s degree and 4 years of experience in Immunology, Cell Biology, Molecular Biology, Pharmacology, Biomedical Sciences, Computational Biology, Bioengineering Preferred Qualifications: Demonstrated hands-on experience independently designing, executing, troubleshooting, and interpreting wet-lab experiments to investigate inflammation biology and validate therapeutic hypotheses. Strong grounding in inflammation and immunology, with the ability to translate computational insights into testable hypotheses and follow-up laboratory studies. Experience analyzing spatial transcriptomics data and/or integrating multimodal omics datasets to investigate disease mechanisms and inform target discovery. Hands-on proficiency in Python or R for omics data analysis and visualization, including the ability to critically evaluate analytical methods and outputs from AI-enabled tools and computational workflows. Ability to work independently and manage defined project components. Strong scientific communication and cross-functional collaboration skills. What you can expect from us As we work to develop treatments that take care of others, we also work to care for your professional and personal growth and well-being. From our competitive benefits to our collaborative culture, we’ll support your journey every step of the way. jobs.title: Associate Scientist
jobs.description: At Bristol Myers Squibb, our employees often ask, “Who are you working for?”—a question that fuels collaboration, accountability, and urgency in our work. Our purpose-driven culture inspires us to discover, develop, and deliver innovative medicines to prevail over serious diseases. We offer uniquely interesting and meaningful work, opportunities for growth, and a supportive environment that values inclusion, wellbeing, flexibility, and comprehensive benefits. This is work that transforms the lives of patients, and the careers of those who do it. Our Chemical Process Development group is a team of organic chemists, analytical chemists, and chemical engineers working together to design novel syntheses from raw materials to supply new medicines to patients. Our scientists focus on developing safe, economical, sustainable, and robust processes to support clinical trials and the launch of new medicines across various drug modalities including small molecules, peptides, oligonucleotides, and antibody drug conjugates. Our work combines innovative science, data-driven decision-making, and cross-functional collaboration to translate laboratory chemistry into reliable manufacturing processes. The scientific and process knowledge generated through development, scale-up, and manufacturing establishes the process understanding, design parameters, and control strategies needed to support regulatory filings and the delivery of new medicines to patients worldwide. Job Summary: The Kilo Lab Scientist plays a key role in translating laboratory-developed chemical processes into safe, robust, and executable manufacturing processes within the New Brunswick Kilo Lab and beyond. Working hands-on with multidisciplinary Chemical Process Development teams, the scientist is responsible for the preparation, scale-up, and execution of processes supporting the manufacture of GMP active drug substance for pharmaceutical development. The scientist leads and coordinates manufacturing campaign activities, including process design and scale-up, equipment selection and setup, materials planning, process safety evaluation review, recipe development, batch execution, equipment cleaning, process documentation, and post-campaign assessment. The role requires a combination of scientific understanding, practical problem-solving, and mechanical aptitude, with a strong commitment to safety, quality, and environmental compliance. Kilo Lab Scientists execute processes from laboratory scale through 200L and work directly with processing equipment throughout campaign preparation and manufacturing. The Kilo Lab also provides an environment for evaluating and implementing emerging manufacturing technologies and methodologies, giving scientists opportunities to contribute to the advancement of how new novel medicines are scaled and manufactured. Responsibilities: Lead the implementation and scale-up of chemical processes from the development laboratory into the New Brunswick Kilo Lab in support of clinical development and GMP active drug substance manufacturing. Work hands-on with chemists, engineers, analytical scientists, and other cross-functional partners to translate laboratory processes into safe, robust, and executable manufacturing operations. Plan, coordinate, and execute Kilo Lab manufacturing campaigns, including equipment selection and setup, raw material planning, process safety readiness, recipe preparation, batch execution, cleaning, and manufacturing documentation. Apply scientific and engineering principles to identify and resolve technical and operational challenges encountered during process scale-up and manufacturing. Review process safety information and translate identified process requirements and operating boundaries into appropriate manufacturing practices. Monitor and assess process performance during manufacturing and document observations, deviations, learnings, and opportunities for process improvement. Ensure manufacturing activities are conducted in accordance with applicable safety, GMP, environmental, and procedural requirements. Collaborate with development teams before and after campaigns to incorporate scale-up and manufacturing learnings into subsequent process development. Participate in the evaluation and implementation of new equipment, manufacturing technologies, and processing methodologies within the Kilo Lab. Contribute to a collaborative working environment through effective communication, knowledge sharing, and partnership across scientific and engineering disciplines. Required Qualifications: BS in Chemistry, Chemical Engineering, or a related scientific or engineering discipline with 1-3 years of experience.*** Demonstrated ability to apply scientific and technical principles to laboratory, process development, scale-up, or manufacturing activities. Strong problem-solving skills and the ability to manage multiple priorities in a dynamic laboratory and manufacturing environment. Ability and willingness to work hands-on with chemical processing equipment and perform activities associated with setup, operation, and execution of manufacturing processes. Strong interpersonal and communication skills with the ability to work effectively across scientific and engineering disciplines in a matrix environment. Ability to work independently, exercise sound technical judgment, and manage assigned activities with appropriate levels of supervision. Commitment to safe working practices, quality, and regulatory compliance. Preferred Qualifications: Advanced degree in Chemistry, Chemical Engineering, or a related scientific or engineering discipline.*** Relevant industry experience in laboratory process development, chemical process scale-up, pilot-scale operations, or pharmaceutical/chemical manufacturing.*** Familiarity with chemical processing equipment and unit operations used in synthetic chemical manufacturing. Knowledge of GMP manufacturing principles and process safety practices. Experience translating laboratory procedures into larger-scale manufacturing operations. Experience with emerging or intensified manufacturing technologies, including continuous or flow processing. Ability and interest in applying and expanding technical capabilities across process development and manufacturing, including supporting Development Engineering laboratory activities and Process Engineering activities associated with externally executed manufacturing campaigns . *** The level of the position will be determined based on the selected candidate’s education, relevant experience, and demonstrated capabilities. The responsibilities described above are representative of the role and are not intended to be an exhaustive list of all responsibilities and activities associated with the position. We hire for skills and capabilities, not just credentials – if this role excites you, but doesn’t perfectly match your resume, we encourage you to apply anyway. Dear Bristol Myers Squibb Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Engineer, IT Compliance opportunity with Bristol Myers Squibb at Bristol Myers Squibb.

But for those who love a challenge, thrive on results, and want to launch a long-term path in sales, it’s incredibly rewarding . If you’re looking to “try out” sales or just dip a toe in, this probably isn’t the role for you. But, if you’re the kind of person who wakes up hungry to compete, thrives on setting and smashing goals, and wants to build a career in tech sales from the ground up — we want to talk to you. At HubSpot, our BDRs are not only the first point of contact for our prospects—they’re also developing the skills and mindset to become our next generation of Account Executives. This is not a placeholder job — it’s the first chapter of a high-growth sales career designed for those who want to build skills, embrace feedback, move fast, and grow even faster. The Role: As an Outbound BDR , you’ll play a key role in HubSpot’s growth engine. You'll be the first touchpoint for many of our future customers, sparking conversations through strategic outreach, uncovering pain points, and qualifying leads. You’ll partner closely with Account Executives to deliver high-quality meetings that drive pipeline, impact, and revenue. Along the way, you’ll sharpen your sales toolkit daily and gain exposure to a world-class sales organization. Compensation & Career Track: This is the first of three levels in our BDR program — designed to take you from prospecting pro to promoting to a full-cycle closer. 💰 Base salary: $53,800 annually 📈 On-target commission: $23,000 annually 🎯 OTE (on-target earnings): $76,800 annually With each promotion, both salary and commission increase — along with your impact. What You’ll Do: Own and execute outbound prospecting through high-volume outreach (60–100+ activities/day) via phone, email, and LinkedIn. Collaborate with Account Executives to target strategic accounts and refine outreach strategy. Qualify leads based on fit, need, and urgency — and book quality discovery meetings. Hit (and exceed) KPIs for activity, meetings delivered, and pipeline impact. Grow fast. Learn fast. Get coached. Apply it. Repeat. What You Won’t Do: Coast. We move fast, we test, we iterate, and we compete. Wait for someone to tell you what to do. We value self-starters who take ownership. Treat this as “just a job.” This is a foundational role, setting you up for a successful long term career in sales. We’re Looking For People Who: ✅ Have 0-2 years of professional sales experience, excluding projects, internships, coursework, bootcamps ✅ Are eager to grow long-term within a sales path–if your focus is split between sales and other paths like customer success, marketing, operations, etc, this role likely won’t be the best fit. ✅ Are resilient, coachable, and crave feedback to improve. ✅ Are curious and ask why, not just how. ✅ Set high standards for themselves — and hit them. ✅ Are technologically fluent, adapting to new technologies and leveraging AI in your day-to-day. ✅ Communicate clearly, write thoughtfully, and can confidently conduct a cold call. ✅ Are energized by a fast-paced environment and a bit of friendly competition. ✅ Either have past sales success or have demonstrated excellence in goal-driven roles (think: fundraising, athletics, service industry, etc). jobs.title: Staff+ Software Engineer, VectorDB
jobs.location: New York City, NY | Seattle, WA; San Francisco, CA | New York City, NY | Seattle, WA
jobs.description: About Anthropic Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems. About the role Anthropic is looking for a Staff+ Software Engineer to work on the vector search infrastructure behind Claude. Retrieval is how Claude learns about the world. Web search across claude.ai, the API and agentic surfaces, memory across conversations, and the reinforcement learning workloads that train our next models all depend on fast, cheap, high-recall nearest-neighbor search over billions of vectors. You'll join a small team responsible for the vector database layer that serves Claude's retrieval workloads: its architecture, performance, scalability and cost. This is a foundational role. The team is small, core architectural decisions are still open, and the engineers who join now will shape how the system evolves. The role sits in our Databases organization and works day to day with the Search Platform team, which owns web search indexing, retrieval and serving, and the Memory & Search team, which owns search and memory inside claude.ai. We're looking for someone who has built vector or search systems that ran in production, at scale, with real users and a real on-call. You'll be hands-on in the code, and you'll also be the person deciding how the pieces fit together. Key responsibilities Own the core of Anthropic's vector database layer: index structures, storage layout, query execution and the serving layer Own production readiness - benchmarking against exact search, capacity planning, onboarding new workloads, and the operational tooling to run it at scale Drive the recall, latency and cost trade-offs - quantization, filtered search, index build and refresh strategy, and how compute and storage are separated and scaled Scale throughput by an order of magnitude as research and training demand grows, and work out whether the bottleneck is architecture, hardware or engineering bandwidth Extend the retrieval stack toward hybrid retrieval - lexical search and fused ranking alongside vector search Set the evaluation methodology for the system - recall targets, latency objectives, cost per query, and the regression detection that keeps them honest Set technical direction for a growing team - lead design reviews, make architectural decisions others build on, and mentor the engineers joining the effort Share the on-call for the systems you own Minimum qualifications Direct experience building a vector database or approximate nearest-neighbor search system that ran in production at scale Deep knowledge of ANN index structures (graph-based, clustering-based or disk-resident approaches), vector quantization and filtered search Experience with search relevance and ranking Strong systems programming skills in a language such as Rust, C++ or Go, including performance-critical and memory-intensive code Experience designing and operating large-scale distributed storage or serving systems with strict latency and reliability requirements A track record of independently scoping and delivering ambiguous, multi-quarter technical projects Strong written and verbal communication, with experience driving alignment across teams with different priorities Interest in AI safety and Anthropic's mission Preferred qualifications Experience with object-storage-backed or disaggregated compute and storage database designs Experience building or operating full-text search engines (inverted indexes, BM25) or hybrid retrieval systems Familiarity with embedding models and the retrieval demands of LLM training and inference Experience using GPUs or other accelerators for index build or search Prior experience as a technical lead on a database or search infrastructure team The annual compensation range for this role is listed below. For sales roles, the range provided is the role’s On Target Earnings ("OTE") range, meaning that the range includes both the sales commissions/sales bonuses target and annual base salary for the role. Annual Salary: $320,000 — $485,000 USD Logistics Minimum education: Bachelor’s degree or an equivalent combination of education, training, and/or experience Required field of study: A field relevant to the role as demonstrated through coursework, training, or professional experience Minimum years of experience: Years of experience required will correlate with the internal job level requirements for the position Location-based hybrid policy: Currently, we expect all staff to be in one of our offices at least 25% of the time. However, some roles may require more time in our offices. Visa sponsorship: We do sponsor visas! However, we aren't able to successfully sponsor visas for every role and every candidate. But if we make you an offer, we will make every reasonable effort to get you a visa, and we retain an immigration lawyer to help with this. We encourage you to apply even if you do not believe you meet every single qualification. Not all strong candidates will meet every single qualification as listed. Research shows that people who identify as being from underrepresented groups are more prone to experiencing imposter syndrome and doubting the strength of their candidacy, so we urge you not to exclude yourself prematurely and to submit an application if you're interested in this work. We think AI systems like the ones we're building have enormous social and ethical implications. We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team. Your safety matters to us. To protect yourself from potential scams, remember that Anthropic recruiters only contact you from @anthropic.com email addresses. In some cases, we may partner with vetted recruiting agencies who will identify themselves as working on behalf of Anthropic. Be cautious of emails from other domains. Legitimate Anthropic recruiters will never ask for money, fees, or banking information before your first day. If you're ever unsure about a communication, don't click any links—visit anthropic.com/careers directly for confirmed position openings. How we're different We believe that the highest-impact AI research will be big science. At Anthropic we work as a single cohesive team on just a few large-scale research efforts. And we value impact — advancing our long-term goals of steerable, trustworthy AI — rather than work on smaller and more specific puzzles. We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills. The easiest way to understand our research directions is to read our recent research. This research continues many of the directions our team worked on prior to Anthropic, including: GPT-3, Circuit-Based Interpretability, Multimodal Neurons, Scaling Laws, AI & Compute, Concrete Problems in AI Safety, and Learning from Human Preferences. Come work with us! Anthropic is a public benefit corporation headquartered in San Francisco. We offer competitive compensation and benefits, optional equity donation matching, generous vacation and parental leave, flexible working hours, and a lovely office space in which to collaborate with colleagues. Guidance on Candidates' AI Usage: Learn about our policy for using AI in our application process.

cold_email.subject: Interest in Rare Cardiac Coordinator — biology/bioinformatics graduate
cold_email.body:
Dear Pfizer Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Rare Cardiac Coordinator opportunity with Pfizer at Pfizer.

I am especially interested in the team's use of quantitative and computational methods to answer meaningful biological questions. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, my background in biology, bioinformatics, Python, R, SQL, Linux, and reproducible workflow development aligns well with that kind of cross-disciplinary work.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. I would be grateful for a 15–20 minute conversation to learn more about the lab's current priorities and discuss where my background could be useful. I have attached my resume for context.

Best,
Celina Lin

cold_email.subject: Interest in Engineer - System Owner — biology/bioinformatics graduate
cold_email.body:
Dear Amgen Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Engineer - System Owner opportunity with Amgen at Amgen.

I am especially interested in the team's use of quantitative and computational methods to answer meaningful biological questions. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, my background in biology, bioinformatics, Python, R, SQL, Linux, and reproducible workflow development aligns well with that kind of cross-disciplinary work.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. I would be grateful for a 15–20 minute conversation to learn more about the lab's current priorities and discuss where my background could be useful. I have attached my resume for context.

Best,
Celina Lin
